correctness.rationale: The frozen L–L exclusion uses an unjustified implication: a single exchange can in principle destroy an adjacent-zero pair and create a disjoint pair next to a different old zero. Restricting the shift to ±1 needs more than the fact that just one zero was lost. The repaired proof verifies all shifts directly and leaves the theorem unchanged. Domination forbids 000, and separation of neighbors forbids two zeros at offset three; these also separate distance-two neighborhoods, and all other neighborhoods are disjoint. The seven-state determinant is checked by its four simple directed cycles and two disjoint pairs. At t=u²,z=w/u its factors are (1−w²)(1−uA−u²B), A=w(1+w⁴), B=w⁴/(1−w²); the coefficients at excesses zero, one and three yield the stated minima, counts and sole n=15 increment. The H and L rotations and exceptional periodic words attain these counts. For n=2m+3, changing vertex coordinates to v=2j turns H zero sets into intervals of length m and the normalized L zero set into {0}∪[2,m−1]∪{m+1}. Intervals overlap in m−1 points just at shifts ±1 in j, yielding ±2 in v. Exactly two intervals overlap the normalized L in m−1 points, [0,m−1] and [2,m+1]; translating back gives L_1 and L_5 from H_0. For an L–L translation by s, symmetry reduces to 1≤s≤m+1 without wrap, giving overlap m−3 at s=1, m−2 at s=2, and at most m+1−s for s≥3 because m is a hole. Thus no L–L exchange occurs. Alternating even codes differ in every coordinate. Each exceptional code keeps at least two of its three disjoint adjacent-zero pairs after one exchange, and two exceptional rotations share at most one zero residue modulo five, so these five are isolated. The odd cycle of H vertices and two neighbors per L give the claimed component and edge counts.
